title: Explain order-to-cash without hiding behind transactions
prompt: Explain the main Order-to-Cash flow and show where master data, pricing, ATP, credit, shipping, billing, and finance responsibilities enter the chain.
expected_points: business purpose and document flow
Business Partner and product master-data influence
pricing as a decision engine
availability and confirmation responsibility
credit as a separate control
shipping and delivery execution boundary
billing and finance handoff identified even if not yet a full Lab vertical
follow_up_questions: Which decisions happen during sales-order creation?
Which result would you investigate first if delivery cannot be created?
red_flags: treats SD as one monolithic component
does not separate physical and financial completion

title: Wrong plant in the sales order
prompt: A sales order receives the wrong delivering plant. How do you investigate the problem without manually overwriting the field?
expected_points: identify plant determination as the target decision
inspect relevant customer, product, sales-area, and plant data
check configuration and rule precedence before document repair
compare expected and actual inputs
prove the first wrong decision and retest the order
follow_up_questions: What downstream processes can a wrong plant affect?
How can the symptom appear later in ATP or shipping?

title: Expected discount is missing
prompt: A customer expects a discount but the sales order does not find it. Describe your diagnostic sequence.
expected_points: confirm pricing procedure and relevant condition types
trace access sequence and condition records
check key fields, validity, scales, currency, units, and exclusion logic
compare document pricing inputs with record keys
separate configuration, master-data, and enhancement causes
prove the fix with pricing trace or equivalent evidence
follow_up_questions: When would you use an enhancement instead of another condition record?
How can pricing differ between order and billing?

title: ATP says no while stock exists
prompt: The warehouse shows stock, but the sales order receives no useful confirmation. Explain how you frame the problem and which assumptions you challenge.
expected_points: separate physical stock from available-to-promise quantity
check scope of check and relevant checking logic
consider requirements, receipts, dates, allocations or protection rules
distinguish classic ATP and advanced ATP capabilities where relevant
trace the confirmation result rather than comparing only stock quantity
follow_up_questions: How can Backorder Processing change a previous confirmation?
What changes when supply protection is used?
red_flags: suggests inventory adjustment before checking demand and scope

title: Explain procure-to-pay as decision layers
prompt: Explain Procure-to-Pay from demand to settlement and separate the main decision layers.
expected_points: demand and requirement source
source determination
purchasing document and item behavior
account assignment
purchasing price and commercial terms
approval and supplier communication
goods or service receipt
invoice verification
GR/IR and financial completion
follow_up_questions: Which layer owns supplier selection?
Why can a process be physically complete but financially incomplete?
red_flags: starts and ends with purchase order
mixes item category and account assignment

title: Wrong supplier selected
prompt: A purchase requisition or purchasing process selects the wrong supplier. What do you check first?
expected_points: confirm source-determination context
inspect source list, quota arrangement, info record, outline agreement, fixed source, validity and blocks as applicable
check plant and purchasing-organization context
separate source selection from price comparison
prove which candidate sources were valid at the decision time
follow_up_questions: When can a fixed source override other candidates?
How can an outline agreement influence the result?
red_flags: checks PO price before source eligibility

title: Goods receipt posted but invoice is blocked
prompt: Goods receipt is complete, but the supplier invoice is blocked or the GR/IR position remains open. How do you investigate?
expected_points: separate physical receipt from invoice verification and financial reconciliation
review PO history and quantities
compare invoice quantity and value with PO and receipt
check tolerance or variance conditions
inspect GR/IR state
identify whether the issue is quantity, price, timing, tax, account assignment, or reference related
follow_up_questions: What evidence proves physical completion?
What evidence proves financial completion?
red_flags: treats GR and invoice as the same event

title: Choose IM or EWM responsibility
prompt: A company needs more warehouse control. How do you decide whether standard inventory management is enough or EWM should own execution?
expected_points: start from required warehouse capabilities rather than product prestige
separate inventory ownership from warehouse execution
consider bins, tasks, waves, labor, automation, handling units, yard or advanced execution needs
consider embedded versus decentralized architecture when EWM is justified
include integration and operational complexity in the decision
follow_up_questions: Which business events stay in ERP?
What additional failure modes appear in decentralized execution?

title: Trace transport demand to settlement
prompt: Trace one outbound transport from ERP demand to freight settlement and name the main ownership changes.
expected_points: transportation demand created from ERP context
freight-unit building
planning and optimizer or manual planning responsibility
freight order or booking
carrier selection or tendering where relevant
execution event ownership
charge calculation
freight settlement handoff back to procurement or finance process
follow_up_questions: Where does EWM enter the execution picture?
Which object is the planning granularity?
red_flags: jumps directly from delivery to carrier invoice
does not distinguish demand, planning, execution, and settlement

title: IDoc, API, event, or file
prompt: An external system must exchange logistics data with S/4HANA. How do you choose between IDoc, API, event, queue, or file integration?
expected_points: start from business interaction and ownership
separate command, query, event, and bulk exchange patterns
consider latency, ordering, volume, replay, coupling, partner capability, and governance
define message identity and idempotency
define error handling and operational ownership
choose technology after the contract and operating model are clear
follow_up_questions: When is an event the wrong choice?
When is a file still a reasonable choice?
red_flags: does not discuss retries or duplicate handling
does not identify system of record

title: Duplicate business document after retry
prompt: An integration timeout causes the sender to retry and a duplicate business document appears. How do you redesign the flow?
expected_points: separate transport retry from business idempotency
introduce stable business or message identity
define duplicate detection at the correct boundary
make retry behavior explicit
decide whether operation is create, upsert, command, or event
add reconciliation and observable status
follow_up_questions: Where should the idempotency key live?
How do you distinguish a safe retry from a new business request?
red_flags: relies only on middleware message ID without business context

title: Synchronous API or asynchronous event
prompt: A sales process needs an external risk or fulfillment decision. Compare a synchronous API call with asynchronous event-driven processing.
expected_points: identify whether the decision is required before business commitment
compare latency and user-experience needs
compare availability coupling and failure behavior
define timeout, fallback, compensation, and stale-data policy
separate a required command or query from notification events
state which system owns the final decision
follow_up_questions: What happens when the external system is unavailable?
Can the process continue with a provisional state?
red_flags: says events are always more modern

title: Design master-data governance ownership
prompt: Several systems can create or change supplier or product data. How do you design governance without turning MDG into a passive replication tool?
expected_points: define data owner and authoritative lifecycle
separate governance workflow from technical distribution
define validation, approval, duplicate prevention, and change responsibility
define which systems can request versus commit master-data changes
design replication and error handling
measure downstream data-quality impact
follow_up_questions: What is the difference between central governance and consolidation?
How do you handle local attributes that should not be centrally owned?
red_flags: focuses on interface technology before data ownership

title: AI recommendation inside a transactional process
prompt: You want AI to recommend how to resolve a sales-order exception. Design the system boundary so AI helps without becoming the uncontrolled system of record.
expected_points: define the business job and exception type
retrieve current business context and evidence
keep transactional state and permissions in the business application
use structured output for recommendation
apply approval for material side effects when risk requires it
log evidence, decision, action, and result
measure business outcome and false-action cost
follow_up_questions: Which actions can be automated safely?
What would you include in an evaluation set?
red_flags: lets the model write directly without controls
does not define authority or rollback

title: RAG or fine-tuning for changing SAP knowledge
prompt: A support assistant must answer from frequently changing internal process and configuration documentation. Compare retrieval with fine-tuning.
expected_points: treat changing knowledge as a retrieval problem first
keep source metadata and access control
use citations or evidence links
evaluate retrieval and answer quality separately
use fine-tuning only for stable behavior gaps rather than document refresh
define freshness and permission tests
follow_up_questions: What can go wrong if old chunks stay in the index?
When could fine-tuning still be useful?
red_flags: uses fine-tuning as a database update mechanism

title: Agent completes the task but chooses a risky path
prompt: An AI agent reaches the expected final result but used an unnecessary write action and bypassed the intended approval path. How do you evaluate and fix the system?
expected_points: evaluate trajectory, not only final answer
reduce tool permissions and allowed actions
make approval state explicit
add policy and deterministic checks around side effects
add negative and adversarial eval cases
log tool calls, state transitions, budgets, and termination reason
follow_up_questions: Which parts should remain deterministic software?
How do you test that the approval cannot be bypassed?
red_flags: solves the issue only with a longer prompt

title: Explain Plan-to-Produce as decisions, not transactions
prompt: Explain the main production planning and execution path from business demand to manufacturing cost settlement. Separate planning, master data, execution, warehouse, quality, and finance responsibilities.
expected_points: demand and planning strategy
MRP and supply proposal
planned order versus production order
production version, BOM, routing and work center roles
component staging and warehouse boundary
operation execution and confirmation
finished-product goods receipt
quality boundary where relevant
actual cost and settlement separated from physical completion
follow_up_questions: What is the first object you inspect if a production order has the wrong components?
Why can a technically complete order still be financially open?
red_flags: starts the process with the production order
treats EWM staging and MRP availability as the same state

title: Production order contains the wrong component structure
prompt: A planned order is converted and the production order contains an unexpected component or operation. How do you find the first wrong decision?
expected_points: freeze material, plant, quantity, planning date and conversion date
check selected production version
check production-version validity and lot-size range
trace BOM alternative and routing assignment
check master-data change between planning and conversion
separate method-selection error from incorrect BOM or routing master data
prove the correction with a clean new planning/conversion test
follow_up_questions: Why is editing the existing production order not enough proof?
What changes if several production methods are valid?
red_flags: edits the order as the first permanent fix
checks only the BOM and ignores production method selection

title: Stock exists but production still waits for a component
prompt: The plant shows enough component stock, but the production line cannot start and EWM is used for production supply. How do you diagnose the gap?
expected_points: confirm the production-order component requirement and required date
separate plant inventory from stock available at the production supply point
check reservation or requirement context
identify production supply area and staging responsibility
inspect EWM staging or warehouse-task state
separate planning shortage from warehouse execution failure
prove completion when the required material reaches the correct production context
follow_up_questions: Which system owns the component requirement and which owns the physical staging?
How would the diagnostic path change without EWM?
red_flags: assumes total plant stock proves production availability
changes MRP parameters before checking warehouse execution

title: MTS, MTO, or engineer-to-order boundary
prompt: A business produces standard products for stock, configurable products for specific customers, and a smaller number of engineered customer solutions. How do you separate MTS, MTO, and ETO without forcing one production model on all three?
expected_points: start from demand ownership and decoupling point
explain general-stock demand for MTS
explain customer-linked requirement and stock/cost context for MTO
identify engineering/project/configuration ownership before executable production for ETO
compare planning stability, lead time, master-data maturity, inventory risk, and customer commitment
define where Sales, engineering/project control, procurement, production and finance hand off
follow_up_questions: Which model creates the highest dependency on stable product master data?
Where would variant configuration or project control enter the discussion?
red_flags: treats MTS, MTO and ETO as order types only
chooses one model only because it is technically possible
does not discuss demand and ownership boundaries
